t: You're looking at the equestrian statue of Viscount Wolseley on Horse Guards Parade. It was made by the Welsh sculptor Sir William Goscombe John and unveiled by the Duke of Connaught in 1920. Garnet Wolseley was an Anglo-Irish officer who became one of Britain's most influential generals after victories in Canada, West Africa and Egypt. The inscription on the back records that he was Field Marshal and Commander-in-Chief of the British Army from 1895 to 1900, and lists his campaigns, from Burma and the Crimea to Egypt and the Sudan.
